Zero regressions confirmed after amend (one macOS CLI suite ran slow — 191s vs. its usual sub-second, a known transient per the project's macOS note — but it still passed clean).

## Report

**STATUS:** DONE

**What I fixed:** `bind_params` in `src/name_resolution/rust_populator/walk/items.rs` was calling `add_locals` once per parameter with a single-element `&[name]` slice, so `add_locals`'s internal `enumerate()` always produced `ordinal = 0` — collapsing every param's `BindingRef` to the same ordinal (an inertness breach vs. parent `48f15d9`, which called `add_locals` once with the full ordered slice).

**Fix:** Restored a single `add_locals` call over the full ordered `(name, def_byte)` slice (preserving `0,1,2,…` ordinals), then loop separately over the collected `(name, LocalFact)` vector calling `b.add_local_fact(file, def_byte, fact)` directly, keyed by def_byte — not routed through a per-name `add_locals` call. I verified the other five `add_locals` call sites (`walk_let`, `walk_closure`, `walk_for`, `walk_match`, `walk_if_while` in `locals.rs`) were never split into per-name calls in `f89dd5c`'s diff — each still passes the full names slice with one shared fact, so ordinals there were never broken.

**Regression tests added** (`src/name_resolution/binding_lookup.rs`, `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`):
1. `param_bindings_get_distinct_ordinals` — `fn f(a: i32, b: i32)` asserts ordinals `(0, 1)`. Verified RED first: failed with `got a=0 b=0` against the reverted buggy code, then GREEN after the fix.
2. `duplicate_same_rib_local_is_ambiguous` — `let x = 1; let x = 2;` in one block, lookup at the trailing `x;` returns `None` (recall-safe ambiguity path, passed even pre-fix — pins existing behavior).

**Test results:** `cargo test --lib name_resolution::binding_lookup::tests` → 3/3 ok; `cargo test --lib` → 274/274 ok; `cargo test --test name_resolution` → 91/91 ok; full `cargo test` → all 28 suites green, zero regressions (one suite took 191s instead of its usual <1s — the documented macOS CLI-test transient, not a failure).

**Other checks:** `cargo fmt` clean, `cargo fmt --check` clean; `cargo clippy --all-targets` — no new warnings in either touched file (all warnings shown are pre-existing, in unrelated files); `cargo build` and `cargo build --features mcp` succeed (pre-existing unrelated `taint.rs` dead-code warnings only); `cargo build --release` + `tier-a --matrix-only --allow-stale-sut` — all matrix cases `ok`/`expected_gap`, 0 regressions.

**Files changed:** `src/name_resolution/rust_populator/walk/items.rs`, `src/name_resolution/binding_lookup.rs`. No file split needed (both well under 600 lines).

**Commit:** amended onto `f89dd5c` (message unchanged) → new SHA **`a16e4cf`**.

**Self-review:** Fix is minimal and scoped exactly to the reported breach; no other files touched; determinism preserved (`BTreeMap` insert-overwrite semantics in `add_local_fact`, ordinals now byte-identical to `48f15d9`); no recall-safety concerns — this fix doesn't touch resolution/lookup logic, only ordinal assignment and fact attachment. Untracked eval/snapshot artifacts left untouched.
